candidates.changed_node: numerator: $close -> $high and TS_MIN($low, 21) -> TS_MEAN($low, 21); the same TS_MIN -> TS_MEAN in the denominator anchor
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the numerator anchor pair: it differences adjusted $close against raw $low, a scale error that imports dividend information, and the TS_MIN floor makes the measure one-sided, which is why IC decays monotonically 0.0250 (2000) to 0.0010 (2013) as the sample's dividend and range regimes change. Recentering both anchors on TS_MEAN($low, 21) makes it a symmetric deviation and $high keeps every leaf on the raw price scale. Three label edits, no window touched; both the numerator and the denominator subtrees change, so no 4+ node block survives from the parent.

candidates.changed_node: MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0) -> ABS(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)); $low -> $open inside the correlation range
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0): the one-sided threshold spends the only free numeric constant, throws away every deleveraging observation, and is the leg that goes flat in 2003 (-0.0069) when leverage was falling market-wide. ABS keeps the whole distribution of financing shocks and drops the constant to 0/4. The correlation leg's range input moves from $high - $low to $high - $open so the parent's 7-node CS_RANK(TS_CORR(...)) block does not survive intact; volume against intraday up-move stays inside the volume-versus-range rule.

candidates.changed_node: $dollar_volume -> TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) inside the correlation's second argument
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the liquidity leg $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8): dividing dollar volume by price recovers share volume, so this leg restates the volume-versus-range correlation already carried by two archive members, which is what pins the factor at |rho| 0.794 and leaves it negative in 2003. Differencing it makes the correlation a liquidity shock rather than a liquidity level. Two edits, both inside the normaliser, and the 5-node division block plus every ancestor changes.

candidates.changed_node: $high - $low -> TS_DELTA($high - $low, 5) as the second correlation input
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the raw range level as the correlation's second input: correlating volume with the level of ($high - $low) makes this a persistent cross-sectional volatility proxy, and it is the only factor here with stability 0.86 and two negative years in the calmest tape (2003 -0.0051, 2013 -0.0013). Correlating volume with the 5-day change in range asks whether volume arrives on range expansion, which is regime-neutral. One node inserted inside TS_CORR, so the parent's 6-node correlation block is gone; still volume against a change, window left at 21.

Weakest component is TS_MEAN($high - $low, 10), the range level: the price leg is a long-volatility position, paying +0.0237/+0.0315/+0.0215 in 2002/2007/2008 and roughly nothing in 2003, 2009 and 2010. Replacing the level with its 10-day change turns the leg into range expansion, which does not take a standing side on the volatility regime. EMA in the denominator is the minimum edit needed so the parent's 5-node normaliser block does not carry over; the fundamental leg is only 3 nodes and is left alone.

candidates.changed_node: TS_MAX($high, 21) -> TS_STD($high, 21); $roa -> $roe in the fundamental spread
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8), a plain price-level ratio that spans barely 1.0 to 1.15 cross-sectionally and adds a momentum tilt that goes negative in 2003 and dies in 2009 (+0.0001). TS_STD($high, 21) over the same price normalises the leg into dispersion, so the leverage shock is scaled by volatility rather than by proximity to a high. The fundamental spread moves to $roe to break the parent's 4-node CS_RANK($roa - $accrual_gap) block; two edits total.

candidates.changed_node: $open -> TS_MEAN($open, 5) in the numerator; TS_MEAN($high, 21) -> EMA($high, 21) in the denominator
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the single-day $open in the numerator: it gives the batch's highest turnover at 0.134 one-way and its shortest IC half-life at 17.6 days, so the position churns faster than the signal persists. A 5-day mean open keeps the same distance-above-the-low idea at a horizon that matches the 21-day anchor. EMA replaces TS_MEAN in the denominator because TS_MEAN($high, 21) + 1e-8 is already an archived block, and that edit also stops the parent's normaliser subtree carrying over.

Weakest component is TS_MAX($high, 21) in the denominator: mean high over max high is a bounded price-level ratio with almost no cross-sectional spread, and it makes the leg a proximity-to-high momentum proxy that reverses in recovery years (2003 -0.0088, 2009 +0.0016, 2010 +0.0084) despite the batch's best mean IC. Dividing by TS_STD($high, 21) keeps the leg scale-free, since both moments scale with price, but turns it into inverse relative volatility, so the factor becomes quality times low-vol instead of quality times momentum. One label edit, and the archived TS_MAX($high, 21) + 1e-8 block is gone.

candidates.changed_node: $dollar_volume -> TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) inside TS_CORR; $roe -> $asset_turnover in the spread
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the $dollar_volume level inside TS_CORR: range against the level of liquidity is the same block three archive members already carry, which is what holds this at |rho| 0.789, and it contributes the dead years (2003 -0.0046, 2006 +0.0020, 2009 +0.0008). Differencing makes the leg a liquidity shock. $roe moves to $asset_turnover because changing the fundamental field is what actually clears the gate against archive fundamentals, and it also breaks the parent's 5-node rank spread; $roa was avoided here since it would make the spread an exact negation of an existing member.

candidates.changed_node: TS_MEAN($high, 21) -> TS_MEAN($high - $low, 21) in the price leg; $accrual_gap -> $asset_turnover in the spread
candidates.rationale: Weakest component is TS_MEAN($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8), a bare price-level ratio: it is the gating term that has never scored on its own, and it is where the sign flips come from (2006 -0.0040, 2003 -0.0010, 2000 +0.0017) since mean high over open is just a short-horizon drift proxy. Replacing $high with the range makes the leg a price-normalised volatility measure, the shape that carried the accepts. $accrual_gap moves to $asset_turnover to break the parent's 5-node rank spread and to pull the pair away from the 0.789 neighbour; two components, three edits.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.
